question: 1. When drafting the Defence of Democracy package of December 2023, did the Commission take account of the rulings of the EU Court of Justice on conditionality, in which the Union’s identity is defined as a European democracy? 2.

Does the Commission endorse the definition of the European Union as a Union of democratic states which also constitutes a democracy of its own, as formulated on 8 March 2024 at the Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam (EU Law Live, Weekend Edition, No. 177)? 3.

Is the Commission prepared to adopt and propagate the definition of the EU as ‘a Union of democratic states which also constitutes a democracy of its own’ in campaigns, such as for the European Parliament elections?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (29.5.2024) Democracy, the rule of law and respect for human rights are founding values of the European Union. The Treaties1 provide that the functioning of the EU shall be founded on representative democracy, and every citizen shall have the right to participate in the democratic life of the EU2. Defending democracy and democratic values is a priority for the Commission3.
In preparing the Defence of Democracy package4, the Commission paid close attention to all relevant caselaw of the Court of Justice of the European Union.

The judgment of 16 February 20225, which ruled that the EU must be able to defend its values within the limits of its powers as laid down by the Treaties, is referred to in the explanatory memorandum accompanying the proposal for a Directive on transparency of interest representation carried out on behalf of third countries6.

The Defence of Democracy package includes two recommendations: a Recommendation on inclusive and resilient elections which includes citizen observers and a Recommendation promoting the engagement of citizens and civil society organisations in public policy-making processes to build democratic resilience. In its external communication, the Commission emphasises promoting democratic values and citizen engagement.

For example, its corporate campaign ‘You are EU’, launched in response to Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, invites all Europeans to stand up for our values and to protect our future. Building on insights acquired during the Conference on the Future of Europe, the Commission has launched innovative tools as part of its democratic ecosystem, including a new generation of citizens’ panels.
It has updated the ‘Have Your Say’ portal, turning it into a digital single-entry point for public consultations, the European Citizens’ Initiative and a new Citizen’s Engagement Platform.

1 Article 2 Treaty on European Union (TEU). 2 Article 10 TEU. 3 Communication on the European Democracy Action Plan, COM(2020) 790 final. 4 https://commission.europa.eu/strategy-and-policy/priorities-2019-2024/new-push-european-
democracy/protecting-democracy_en 5 Hungary v European Parliament and Council, Case C-156/21, ECLI:EU:C:2022:97. 6 COM(2023) 637 final.
